public_solution_overlap.prior_art: Native SQLite ALTER already solves ordinary dependency-aware renames. Open PR703 solves an incoming-FK transform case. PR499 attempts FTS trigger recreation, and PR854 documents current trigger deletion and stale view references. This task composes native operations with actual table rebuilds, literal/default/conversion semantics, dependency preservation, isolated data-validating preview, and atomic multi-table outcomes; none of those narrow fixes alone is the task.
public_solution_overlap.audit_limit: Pinned source, relevant current issue/PR pages and source behavior were inspected. No exhaustive absence claim across forks or unpublished solutions.
public_solution_overlap.runtime_qualification: SQLite3.53.0 already adds native NOT NULL/CHECK alteration. This frozen task uses the recorded SQLite3.40.1 verifier runtime, so nullability handling is partly older-runtime compatibility. The original contribution is the composed transformation/validation contract; current native rename and constraint alteration are not claimed as new.

contract_scope.supported: Main-schema ordinary rowid tables; primary/composite keys unchanged but renameable; self/cyclic/composite FKs and their actions/deferrability; native-accepted rename/drop dependency rewrites; type/default/nullability/order/STRICT rebuilds; quoted identifiers; literal defaults; hidden rowids and AUTOINCREMENT; indexes/triggers/views; read-only dry-run snapshots.
contract_scope.excluded: Selected generated/virtual/WITHOUT ROWID tables or tables shadowing every hidden rowid alias; primary-key type/nullability changes; calls within existing transactions; TEMP/attached schemas; custom functions/collations; ambiguous dependencies rejected by native SQLite. No guarantee of bounded memory or performance on arbitrarily large databases.
contract_scope.reason: Keep a complete useful composed operation while preserving native SQLite semantics. Requiring an arbitrary general SQL parser or promising all virtual-table modules would manufacture additional complexity.

verifier.behavioral_evidence: Combined changes across related tables; trigger/index/view writes after migration; typed conversions and rollback; preserved rowids/high-water marks; composite/cyclic deferrable FKs; exact dry-run/reality reports; source bytes including WAL unchanged during readonly preview; busy writer failure; process death after first rebuild with hot-journal recovery; supported connection modes and pragma restoration.

horizon.hypothesis: Sustained work may arise from coordinating native rename/drop stages, lossless existing column definitions, explicit data conversion, full-table copy identity, dependent object recreation, sequence state, transaction settings, dry-run snapshots and CLI/API behavior. A rename-only patch or ordinary transform wrapper fails concrete composed behavior. Neither test count nor patch length measures agent steps; >=75 steps remains unvalidated.
